blockers.quote: At work, you start calling it. That review's fake. Those are bots. Right every time.
blockers.why: No new power rule after halfway fails. A dot marks machine-written words whether a person sent them or not; it cannot identify a fake review or distinguish bots from tired people.
blockers.fix: At work, you start calling it. That review was machine-written. So were those comments. Who pressed send? The dot won't tell you.

blockers.quote: > SCENE: The office, morning. Your screen: the reviews of the restaurant downstairs, five stars each, a dot on each. Then your cousin's video in the group chat, lilac head waving from a window; the comments under it scroll past as a field of red. Then the office floor: you at your desk, pointing at a screen; coworkers turning; your boss, grey-blue head, tie, at his glass door, watching.
blockers.why: No new person after 60% fails. The cousin first appears at 6:28, after roughly 60% of the 9:55 runtime.
blockers.fix: Plant the cousin's lilac-head birthday video in the Detective montage at line 102, then make this appearance its return.

blockers.quote: And then you look up, and it was never just your phone.
blockers.why: Check #5, But / therefore, fails at the transition from the personal cost to the wider consequence; this is explicitly an “and then” connection.
blockers.fix: But when you look up, it was never just your phone.

suggestions.quote: Her instruction. Yours. Two machines, told the same thing by two people who were asleep, booked a cafe.
suggestions.fix: At line 154, visibly plant assistant permissions to message contacts and add calendar events, so the cafe booking reads as payoff rather than unexplained capability.

suggestions.quote: That's what happens when a birthday wish is specific.
suggestions.fix: You asked who meant it. The candle answered the easier question.

suggestions.quote: Those are the people typing. Everyone else is asleep, or working, or scared of getting it wrong.
suggestions.fix: Those are the people typing. The dark windows hide everything a dot cannot tell you: asleep, working, scared—or nobody at all.

keep.quote: But a dot says who wrote it. It never says why. Remember that.
She was keeping you with the only hours she had left: the ones she was asleep for.
Nobody wrote it. Both of you meant it.
